items.headline: Jantar Mantar pair freed; UN experts seek probe
items.text: A Delhi magistrate on Wednesday ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, jailed over a Jantar Mantar protest, rejecting a police request for three more days' custody. On Tuesday two dozen UN experts urged an independent inquiry into force used at the protests; India has said police acted strictly in accordance with the law.

photo.alt: A tall red and beige stone instrument with arched openings, on a lawn.
photo.caption: The Jantar Mantar observatory in New Delhi. The road beside it was the capital's main protest site until police denotified it this month.

items.headline: Century-old Delhi mosque told to vacate
items.text: The Land and Development Office told the Race Course mosque near the Prime Minister's residence to vacate within six days, calling it unauthorised on government land; the Delhi Waqf Board says it is Waqf property notified in 1977. Nearly 700 nearby families were displaced; police say they were given homes in Mundka.

items.headline: Tear gas in Imphal; Kuki man shot dead
items.text: Police fired tear gas on Wednesday as protesters over Monday's killing of three Meitei firewood collectors tried to enter an Imphal event attended by the Chief Minister; three people had minor injuries. A Kuki man, Paolen Khongsai, was shot dead on Tuesday. Police have arrested three suspects in Monday's ambush.

photo.alt: Women vendors selling vegetables, fish and grain on the floor of a covered market, seen from above.
photo.caption: Ima Keithel, the women's market in central Imphal.

items.headline: Court summons Srinagar magistrate over PSA order
items.text: The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court ordered Srinagar's District Magistrate to appear in person with the full record and explain why he allegedly passed a Public Safety Act detention order against Zubair Amin Bangroo 'recklessly and mechanically'. The order alleges links to militants; the authorities' reply is not reported.

items.headline: Abyei market strike toll rises to 153
items.text: Abyei's caretaker information minister says Monday's drone strike on Amiet Market killed at least 153 people, up from 73, with fires still burning; MSF is treating more than 20 wounded. South Sudan blames Sudan's army. A senior Sudanese officer told AP the army hit RSF-bound fuel tankers and does not target civilians.

photo.alt: Flat, dry savannah dotted with trees and round huts, seen from an aircraft window.
photo.caption: Abyei and the surrounding plain, seen from a UN helicopter.

items.headline: Police clear Portugal housing-protest camps
items.text: Police cleared cost-of-living protest camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square before dawn and arrested 55 people, released pending a court appearance; protesters returned within hours, and organisers count over 1,000 at each camp in Lisbon and Porto. Police called the eviction 'calm, proportionate'; a camp spokesperson called it 'very aggressive'.

items.headline: Burkina Faso restores the death penalty
items.text: Burkina Faso's unelected transitional parliament unanimously adopted a penal code restoring the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, espionage and other crimes, Human Rights Watch reports; it had been abolished for ordinary crimes in 2018. The justice minister called it a necessary measure to combat terrorism.

items.headline: UN experts: fate of returned North Koreans unknown
items.text: UN-appointed experts said the fate of many people forcibly returned to North Korea from China since 2023 is unknown, citing risks of disappearance, torture and forced labour, and urged China to stop the returns. The UN report carries no response from China or North Korea.

focus.title: Sudan's long war
focus.dek: Since 15 April 2023, fighting between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has killed at least 59,000 people by one count, and possibly far more, and driven about 13 million from their homes. Both sides deny targeting civilians. The war now reaches into Abyei and South Sudan.
focus.alt: Women in long robes and headscarves walk across sandy ground carrying bags and boxes of supplies on their heads and in their arms, with more people behind them.
